excluded_papers.title: Day-ahead electricity price forecasting with high-dimensional structures: Univariate vs. multivariate modeling frameworks
excluded_papers.reason: Pure price-only study: Section 4 explicitly excludes exogenous variables "like weather, load or renewable energy generation forecasts"; all 58 models use only lagged prices and deterministic calendar dummies, so no weather/NWP/renewable-forecast inputs exist to audit.

excluded_papers.title: One-week-ahead electricity price forecasting using weather forecasts, and its application to arbitrage in the forward market: an empirical study of the Japan Electric Power Exchange
excluded_papers.reason: Forecast horizon is one week ahead (weekly-average JEPX spot price, decided in week t-1 for forward-market arbitrage), not day-ahead(ish) EPF; coded columns retained for reference since gate-vintage alignment is explicit.

excluded_papers.title: Understanding electricity prices beyond the merit order principle using explainable AI
excluded_papers.reason: Explicitly not forecasting: "we will not make predictions in the sense of a forecast"; ex-post XAI explanation with weekly-shuffled (non-chronological) splits and post-clearing auction outcomes (day-ahead total scheduled generation, import/export) as inputs — not day-ahead-horizon EPF.

excluded_papers.title: Hybrid Kolmogorov-Arnold Network and XGBoost Framework for Week-Ahead Price Forecasting in Australia's National Electricity Market
excluded_papers.reason: Horizon is week-ahead, not day-ahead: H = 168 hourly steps from a 336-hour look-back, and the paper positions itself explicitly against day-ahead work — "Although day-ahead forecasting has been widely studied in the NEM, week-ahead hourly forecasting remains relatively underexplored despite its practical importance" (Sec. I, p.1). It IS genuine electricity PRICE forecasting (RRP) with weather-derived inputs (temperature, wind speed, humidity, cloud cover) plus AEMO renewable generation forecasts, so it fails only the horizon criterion. Compounding this, the Australian NEM is a real-time dispatch market settled at five-minute resolution with rebidding, so there is no day-ahead auction and no day-ahead bidding gate against which input admissibility could be assessed. Columns are coded anyway as a near-miss/borderline record: the paper is a clean instance of the availability-timing gap, naming weather variables and renewable "forecasts" while never stating their vintage, publication time, or availability at the forecast origin.

excluded_papers.title: The Evolution of Probabilistic Price Forecasting Techniques: A Review of the Day-Ahead, Intra-Day, and Balancing Markets
excluded_papers.reason: review, not a primary study — reports no empirical experiment of its own (no dataset, no case study, no numerical results); additionally uses no weather-derived inputs, since it conducts no forecasting.
